He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, reminding him of His blessings upon him and His kindness to him, urging him through this to be thankful for what He has bestowed on him, so that he may thereby deserve more of it: ﴿Did We not expand for you﴾, O Muhammad, for guidance, faith in God and knowledge of the truth, ﴿your breast?﴾ So We softened your heart and made it a vessel for wisdom. ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾: that is, We forgave you what had preceded of your sins and lifted from you the weight of the days of ignorance (jahiliyyah) in which you were. It is also said that in the recitation (qira'ah) of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), as reported, it reads: ﴿And We removed from you your burden (wizr?) which had weighed down your back﴾, where the word is wiqrak; the meaning is: that which made your back heavy and weakened it. This is from their saying about a camel when it returns from a journey, weakened by the journey and its flesh gone: it is naqd safar (the wear of travel).

Those who engaged in ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾, he said: your sin. ﴿Which had weighed down your back﴾, he said: it made your back heavy.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed down your back﴾: the Prophet ﷺ had sins that had weighed him down, and God forgave them to him.

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿which had weighed down your back﴾, he said: the Prophet had sins that had weighed him down, and God forgave them to him.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾, meaning: the polytheism (shirk) that he was in.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden﴾: He expanded his breast for him and forgave him the sin he had committed before he was made a prophet, and so He lifted it.

And regarding His words: ﴿which had weighed down your back﴾, he said: He made it heavy and burdensome, as a heavy load weakens a camel until it becomes emaciated after having been fat. ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾, he said: your sin which had weighed down your back, made your back heavy; We removed it from you and lightened for you what had weighed down your back.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾:

That is: We raised high your remembrance, so that I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned along with Me. This is His saying: "There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God."

Those who engaged in ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Abu Kurayb and Amr ibn Malik told us, both saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, he said: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with Me: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God."

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾, he said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Begin with ʿubūdah (servitude to God), and follow with risalah (messengership)." I said to Ma'mar: [what is meant is:] he says: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant," which is ʿubūdah, and "His messenger," which is that you say: "His servant and His messenger."

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance﴾: God raised his remembrance in this world and the Hereafter; there is no preacher, nor one who recites the testimony (tashahhud), nor one who prays, but he proclaims: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God."

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that he said: "Gabriel came to me and said: 'Indeed my Lord and your Lord says: How have I raised high your remembrance?' * *

As for His words: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Indeed, along with the hardship in which you are, from striving against these polytheists, and at its beginning what you are upon, there is hope and relief, that He will give you victory over them, until they submit to the truth you have brought them, willingly or unwillingly.

Those who said so:

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard Yunus say: al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Rejoice, ease has come to you. Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Uliyya told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, the like of it, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Awf told us, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet ﷺ, in similar terms.

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, who said: The Prophet ﷺ went out one day, joyful and happy, laughing, and he was saying: "Hardship will never overcome two eases, hardship will never overcome two eases." ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾: it was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God ﷺ gave his companions glad tidings of this verse, and said: "Hardship will never overcome two eases."

Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra Abu Iyas, from a man, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "If hardship entered a hole, ease would come and enter upon it, because God says: ﴿So indeed, with hardship comes ease. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Shu'bah, from a man, from Abdullah, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, with hardship comes ease﴾, he said: ease follows hardship.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾

The people of ta'wil differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: when you finish your prayer, then labor (infsab) in supplication (du'a'), and ask your Lord for your needs.

Those who said so:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾, he says: in supplication.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾, he says: when you are free from what has been obligated upon you of prayer, then ask God, and turn eagerly to Him, and labor for Him.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Warqa told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾, he said: when you stand for prayer, then labor in your need before your Lord.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾, he says: from the obligatory prayer before you give the salam, then labor.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor, and to your Lord direct your longing﴾: he was commanded, when he was free from his prayer, to strive earnestly in his supplication.

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free﴾ from your prayer ﴿then labor﴾ in supplication.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿So when you are free﴾ from fighting your enemy, ﴿then labor﴾ in the worship of your Lord.

Those who said so:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said regarding His words: ﴿So when you are free, then labor﴾: he was commanded, when he was free from his military campaign, to strive earnestly in supplication and worship.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: when you are free from the affairs of your worldly life, then labor in the worship of your Lord.

Those who said so:

* *

As for His words: ﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And to your Lord, O Muhammad, direct your longing, not to anyone else of His creation, since these polytheists of your people have directed their longing in their needs to the idols and rivals.

Those who engaged in ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mahran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾, he said: make your intention and your longing toward God.

Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾, he said: make your longing and your intention toward your Lord.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And to your Lord direct your longing﴾, he said: when you stand for prayer.

**End of the commentary on Surah Alam Nashrah.**
